batchName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476) - Easy Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476)

questions.question: What was the great Roman innovation in wall painting?
questions.explanation: Romans painted gardens in flower, city views and scenes from the Odyssey. They even used an early form of perspective.
questions.sourceQuote: The great Roman innovation was landscape: gardens in flower, views of city buildings and scenes from the Odyssey, the Greek epic of a hero's voyage home, using an early form of perspective.

questions.question: What made water flow through Roman aqueducts?
questions.explanation: Aqueducts followed gentle downward slopes all the way to the city. Most of their channels ran underground.
questions.sourceQuote: Aqueducts carried water to cities by gravity alone, along gentle downward slopes.

questions.question: Roughly how many spectators could the Colosseum hold?
questions.explanation: Completed around AD 80, the Colosseum had retractable awnings for shade. It staged gladiator fights and even mock sea battles.
questions.sourceQuote: It held over 50,000 spectators, had retractable awnings for shade, and staged gladiator fights and even mock sea battles.

questions.question: What volcanic ash made Roman concrete unusually strong?
questions.explanation: Pozzolana was mixed with lime mortar, water and rubble. The resulting opus caementicium was poured into reusable wooden frames.
questions.sourceQuote: Roman concrete (*opus caementicium*) mixed lime mortar, water and rubble with pozzolana, a volcanic ash that made it unusually strong.

questions.question: Which powerful people of central Italy, living just north of Rome, were among the earliest influences on Roman art?
questions.explanation: Roman art began as a borrower, drawing first on the Etruscans and on the Greek colonies of southern Italy. The Etruscans had themselves learned much from their Greek trading partners.
questions.sourceQuote: Its earliest influences came from the Etruscans, a powerful people of central Italy north of Rome, and from the Greek colonies of southern Italy.

questions.question: The Arch of Constantine honours the emperor under whom which religion triumphed?
questions.explanation: The arch was completed around AD 315 near the Colosseum. It mixes older classical roundels with new, squat-figured panels.
questions.sourceQuote: It was built for Constantine, the emperor under whom Christianity triumphed, and it combines older carved roundels in the full classical style with new panels of squat, hard-edged figures.

questions.question: What was the forum, the heart of every Roman town?
options: An open square for market, meetings and debate
questions.explanation: The forum served as market, meeting place and political stage. In Rome, the original Forum was later joined by grander imperial forums.
questions.sourceQuote: The heart of every Roman town was its forum, an open square serving as market, meeting place and stage for political debate.

questions.question: What was the hypocaustum in a Roman bathhouse?
questions.explanation: Hot air from a furnace flowed beneath raised floors and through gaps in the walls. It was a forerunner of central heating.
questions.sourceQuote: Rooms were warmed by underfloor heating (*hypocaustum*), which sent hot air from a furnace beneath raised floors and through gaps in the walls, a forerunner of central heating.

questions.question: Which volcano's eruption in AD 79 preserved the painted rooms of Pompeii and Herculaneum?
questions.explanation: Ash from Vesuvius buried these wealthy towns on the Bay of Naples. That disaster is why most surviving Roman painting is wall painting.
questions.sourceQuote: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79, ash buried Pompeii and Herculaneum, wealthy towns on the Bay of Naples, preserving their decorated rooms.

questions.question: Why has almost all of the most prestigious Roman painting been lost?
options: It was painted on cloth that was reused
It was destroyed by order of Christian emperors
It was melted down for its gold pigments
It was painted on wooden panels, which rot
questions.explanation: Romans prized panel painting most, but wood decays over time. What survives is mostly wall painting.
questions.sourceQuote: The most prestigious kind was painted on wooden panels, and wood rots.
